inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-02T21:59:47Z NZX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime); 52w range 7.55-9.28, price at ~90th percentile of the 10-year monthly range
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built, identical in all three scenarios. Cost of equity 10.9% = NZ 10y govt ~4.5% (Sept-2026, assumed; refresh) + equity beta 0.80 x ERP 5.5% (asset beta ~0.70 for a monopoly port/infrastructure asset with stable volume-linked revenue, re-levered at 12% D/V - deliberately BELOW a generic NZ small-cap beta of ~1.1-1.3 because port throughput is far less cyclical than the typical NZX small-cap) = 8.9%, PLUS +1.5% small-cap illiquidity / minority-holder premium (market cap NZ$234m, Environment Southland holds 66% so the true float is ~NZ$80m, thin trading, no realistic takeover premium), PLUS +0.5% single-asset / single-region premium (one port, one Southland catchment, undiversifiable at the company level). Tiwai/NZAS customer concentration is NOT added to WACC: the curtailment risk is charged ONCE, in the bear-case flows (FY27 -6% revenue, 37% margin) and in the 25% bear weight (owner-fcf.md s7f - risk lives in the flows OR the rate, never both). After-tax cost of debt 3.9% (FY26 interest 1.66m / 31.0m gross debt = 5.4% pre-tax x (1-0.28)). Weights at market: E 88.3% / D 11.7%. WACC = 0.883 x 10.9 + 0.117 x 3.9 = 10.08%, rounded to 10.0%. Cross-check: the 'standard' 11-12% NZ small-cap rate in the sanity-check template would apply if the beta were ~1.2; the lower rate here is the honest offset for infrastructure stability that the brief asked to be weighed, and the required_return_table shows the 11-12% answers ($5.5-4.9) for the reader who disagrees.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US/cyclical row, section 7 adaptations). South Port is a profitable, cash-generative, capital-intensive infrastructure operator whose value IS its stream of free cash flow; it is not a REIT (assets at historic cost, no fair-value noise), not a bank, not an LIC, and there is no live corporate action. Fresh build - no prior SPN.NZ DCF, no memory entry.
OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 14.159 - SBC 0.148 - interest income 0 (not stripped, net-debt company) = 14.011. No IFRS-16 or NCI adjustment (none material).

MID-CYCLE / PEAK CHECK: FY2026 is a company-declared record year following the curtailment-depressed FY2025. FY2026 owner FCF 14.011 is 2.2x the FY2019-26 median (6.375) - a raw peak flag - but the dollar median is depressed by the FY2022-24 channel-deepening capex supercycle (capex 50% of revenue in FY2022) and by 63% revenue growth over the window, so the raw series is not a fair test. On a normalised-capex basis (OCF less 13.4% of revenue, the 10-year median capex ratio) the FY2026 FCF margin is 19.5% vs an 8-year median of 17.4% (1.12x). The component build therefore starts FY2027 at a 17.8% owner-FCF margin (revenue +1% on guided flat volumes and the loss of wind-farm project cargo; EBITDA margin 40.0% vs 41.6% actual as management invests in people and maintenance; capex 13% of revenue vs 13.1% actual) - i.e. year-1 FCF of $12.9m is the mid-cycle figure, 8% below FY2026 actual, and no separate fcf_base override is needed. The dashboard engine rebuilds it from these drivers.

CAPEX: modelled at 13.0% of revenue in the base (10-year median 13.4%, mean 18.5%; ~1.7x D&A of 7.8%). This deliberately embeds a continuing growth-capex layer: the 30-year Port Planning Exercise (Stages 1-2 due late Sept 2026) plus a flagged tug and mobile-harbour-crane replacement make a new capex cycle likely, and the 3-4% revenue growth modelled has to be paid for. Bear uses 14% (capex cycle with a weak volume payoff), bull 11.5% (channel deepening complete, landside productivity gains).

WORKING CAPITAL: net working capital ~5% of revenue (receivables 8.1 vs payables 4.6); modelled as -5% capture on the CHANGE in revenue (growth absorbs cash). Contract liabilities (~2.1m, Tiwai prepaid wharfage) are stable and not modelled as a tailwind.

TAX: 28% NZ statutory on EBIT throughout. FY2026 cash tax paid 5.358 on PBT 22.91 (23.4%) lags the provision by timing only; no losses or credits. Building-depreciation non-deductibility since FY2024 means cash tax will not fall below the provision.

TERMINAL: Gordon growth at 2.25% (base) / 2.5% (bull) / 1.5% (bear) - at or below long-run NZ nominal GDP for a mature single-region asset. Exit-multiple cap per Step 8c.5(4) in EV/EBITDA terms: bear 8.12x (10y min), base 9.92x (10y avg), bull 11.41x (10y max); terminal_cap_multiple is the SAME cap restated as a multiple of terminal-year owner FCF so the dashboard slider engine and the eval hurdle check (both cap on FCF_N) reproduce it exactly. Gordon binds in every scenario - the caps do not bite.

DIVIDEND STOCK: 47% payout, 29cps fully imputed (net yield 3.25%, gross 4.5% at $8.92). The DCF values the whole FCF stream, of which the dividend is roughly half; the balance has historically been reinvested in growth capex at (per management) at least a WACC return.
PRICE: regular NZX close, not after-hours. $8.92 is 4% below the 52-week high and near the top of the 10-year range; the FY26 record result (21-Aug-2026) is already in the price.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Owner-FCF CAGRs (SBC-adjusted; SBC is 0.1-0.2% of revenue so adjusted and reported series are within 1% of each other). Both are meaningless as growth anchors: the FY2023 base is a capex-supercycle trough (1.425) and the FY2021 base pre-dates it. Use the revenue and volume CAGRs.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case through-cycle revenue path: 10-year cargo-volume CAGR 2.65% plus ~1% price/mix; the 5-year equity CAGR of 8.7% is not divergent from revenue (8.7%) or EPS (8.4%) but all three 5-year figures span a curtailment trough to a declared record year and management guides FY2027 volumes flat, so they are not carried forward.
historical_growth.notes: Equity CAGR (8.7% 5y) tracks revenue and EPS - no >30% divergence. Owner-FCF CAGR is not materially below reported FCF CAGR (SBC immaterial). Volumes: 3.05m t (FY2016) -> 3.96m t (FY2026); FY2026 includes ~16k t of one-off wind-farm project cargo and a wind-throw log surge.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 revenue +1%: volumes guided 'broadly in line with FY26' with the 16k-tonne wind-farm project cargo gone and log volumes normalising after the FY26 wind-throw surge, offset by tariff inflation and a full year of the MSC Eagle service and the Bluff Freight Centre. EBITDA margin eases to 40.0% (management: 'invest more in our people and infrastructure') then settles at 40.5%, the 10-year mean. Growth 4-4.5% in FY28-30 as the Southland wind pipeline (1,851MW consented/in development) delivers lumpy project cargo, Edendale dairy warehousing ramps and Tiwai runs at full three-potline output, fading to 2.5% by FY36. Capex 13% of revenue funds a moderate Port-Planning capex programme (tug, crane, landside). Tiwai stays open to 2044 with no curtailment beyond a normal dry-year nuisance.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tiwai runs uninterrupted, the wind-farm pipeline converts into 5-8 years of recurring project cargo, container volumes keep compounding on the new MSC services, and Ballance coastal fertiliser shifts to Bluff after the Mt Maunganui closure. Revenue +6% FY28-29, fading to 3%. Operating leverage on a fixed-cost port takes EBITDA margin to 43.5% (the FY2022 peak). Channel deepening is complete so capex runs at 11.5% of revenue (landside productivity, not marine works). Terminal growth 2.5%. Requires three independent things to go right - Tiwai, project cargo AND margin - hence only 25% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: A repeat Meridian demand-response call on NZAS (up to 185MW available under the 2024 agreements) in a dry FY27/28 cuts Tiwai tonnage by a third for a season, China log demand stays weak, and dairy payout cuts trim farm-input imports: FY27 revenue -6%, EBITDA margin 37% (below the FY2024 trough of 38%). The Port Planning Exercise then launches a transformation capex cycle (14% of revenue) whose volume payoff is slow, under a new CEO and Chair. Recovery to 2-2.5% growth from FY29; margin never exceeds 38.5%; terminal growth 1.5%. Not a solvency case - net debt/EBITDA stays under 2x and the dividend is cut, not suspended.

bear.market_multiple_reference_note: MEMO, not the house value: same flows, terminal value at the stock's own 10-year average EV/EBITDA (9.92x) instead of Gordon growth. The gap to intrinsic_value is the price of assuming the market never de-rates this asset from its historical multiple.

base.market_multiple_reference_note: MEMO, not the house value: same flows, terminal value at the stock's own 10-year average EV/EBITDA (9.92x) instead of Gordon growth. The gap to intrinsic_value is the price of assuming the market never de-rates this asset from its historical multiple.

bull.market_multiple_reference_note: MEMO, not the house value: same flows, terminal value at the stock's own 10-year average EV/EBITDA (9.92x) instead of Gordon growth. The gap to intrinsic_value is the price of assuming the market never de-rates this asset from its historical multiple.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected owner FCF for 10 years and exiting at a terminal value BUILT AT THE 15% HURDLE (min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF_10), not the WACC-built TV) returns a 15% IRR; net debt deducted; per scenario then probability-weighted.
entry_price.note: Weighted entry price $3.51 is -60.6% below the current price and ~55% of weighted IV - the expected relationship when a 15% hurdle is demanded from an asset discounted at 10% (owner-fcf.md s4 sanity property). At $8.92 the base path returns roughly 8% IRR (see required_return_table).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_10)). The 10% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. The current price of $8.92 sits between the 8% and 9% rows - the market is pricing the base path at roughly an 8% return, consistent with how NZ income investors have historically valued this stock (10y avg EV/EBITDA 9.9x).

sensitivity.note: rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; each cell rebuilds and re-caps the terminal value at that WACC/g pair

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: a single customer is 24% of tonnage with a proven, recurring curtailment mechanism (Feb-2025 event), FY27 is guided flat with an explicit project-cargo cliff and no firm numbers, a new capex cycle is about to be sized (Port Planning Exercise, late Sept 2026), and CEO + Chair both changed within six months. Bull cut to 25%: it needs Tiwai stability, wind-farm cargo conversion AND a return to the FY2022 peak margin simultaneously, and the stock already trades near its 10-year high so there is no valuation slack for disappointment. Not raised further because the balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.6x, $19m headroom) removes solvency from the bear case.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street values differ by ~$0.07/share because SBC is 0.2% of revenue - the accounting-regime band has collapsed to a point and band_position is reported as null rather than a degenerate number. The price sits ABOVE both the house and street weighted values.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.outlier_excluded: FY2024 excluded from the P/E average only: reported NPAT $7.376m carried a one-off $2.3m deferred-tax expense from the March-2024 removal of tax depreciation on commercial buildings (normalised NPAT $9.956m, P/E 15.8x on that basis). FY2024 stays in the P/B, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales averages because those are unaffected by the tax item.

price_range_10y.note: monthly closes Jun-2017..Aug-2026; 52w 7.55-9.28; current 8.92 is in the upper half (~90th percentile)

peak_earnings_test.note: The raw-dollar test trips (2.2x) but is distorted by the FY2022-24 capex supercycle and 63% revenue growth over the window; on a normalised-capex margin basis FY2026 is 1.12x the median. The model does not carry FY2026 forward: year-1 owner FCF is built at $12.9m (17.8% margin), 8% below FY2026, from a 40% EBITDA margin, 13% capex and +1% revenue. This IS the Step 8c.5(1) mid-cycle rebuild, expressed through the driver paths so the dashboard engine reproduces it.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip in the over-valuation direction. Base IV $6.31 implies P/E 10.4x vs a 10-year ex-outlier average of 17.2x (range 14.0-19.4x), P/B 2.2x vs max 4.52x, EV/EBITDA 6.19x vs max 11.41x, and upside is negative (-29.2%). The implied multiples sit BELOW every level the market has paid for this stock in ten years. The finding runs the other way: the current price ($8.92, P/E 14.7x, EV/EBITDA 8.49x) is itself at the LOW end of the stock's historical multiple range, and the market has consistently capitalised this asset at ~10x EBITDA / ~17x earnings, i.e. at a ~8% discount rate. The DCF at 10% WACC says that rate is too generous for a NZ$80m-float, single-region, single-anchor-customer port with a capex cycle about to be announced; the required_return_table and market_multiple_reference_iv make the disagreement explicit rather than hiding it.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required by the trip tests. Conservative structure applied pre-emptively: (1) mid-cycle year-1 FCF via the component build (see peak_earnings_test); (2) WACC 10.0% including +2.0pp of documented structural premiums (illiquidity/66%-council-held float +1.5, single-asset/region +0.5) on a 0.80 infrastructure beta, with Tiwai concentration charged once in the bear flows and 25% bear weight rather than stacked into the rate; (3) terminal growth 2.25% base / 1.5% bear, at or below long-run NZ GDP; (4) exit_multiple_cap per scenario (bear 8.12x / base 9.92x / bull 11.41x EV/EBITDA) - recorded, but Gordon growth binds in every scenario so the caps do not change any value.
sanity_check.sbc_note: SBC is $0.148m (0.2% of revenue) in FY2026, $0.106m FY2025, $0.036m FY2024, nil before. SBC-adjusted and reported multiples differ by <1% on both sides of the comparison - no adjusted/unadjusted mixing. Historical P/E uses diluted EPS less SBC/share; will not match Yahoo's GAAP P/E.
sanity_check.direction_of_conclusion: The DCF finds SPN.NZ EXPENSIVE at $8.92: weighted IV $6.32 (-29.1%), base $6.31, and even the bull case ($8.50) is below the price. The stock is priced as a bond-like income asset at ~8% required return with its historical ~10x EBITDA multiple held in perpetuity; on a 15% hurdle the buy-below price is $3.51.

detail.method: June monthly close from Yahoo (10y, 1mo bars) x 26.2349m shares; EV = market cap + (total debt - cash) at FY-end; P/E on diluted EPS less SBC/share; FY2026 debt corrected to 31.008 (current + non-current).

valuation_philosophy.model_choice: Owner-FCF DCF, ten-year explicit build from components (revenue x EBITDA margin - SBC - D&A -> 28% tax + D&A - capex - working capital), Gordon terminal value with an EV/EBITDA exit cap, three probability-weighted scenarios at a single 10% NZD WACC. Chosen because South Port is an operating infrastructure company whose cash flows are real, recurring and largely volume-linked; every non-FCF model in the routing table (AFFO, residual income, NAV) would mis-describe a port that carries its wharves at historic cost and pays out half its earnings.
valuation_philosophy.mid_cycle_choice: FY2026 is a declared record following a curtailment-depressed FY2025, so the base year is NOT carried forward. Year-1 owner FCF ($12.9m, 17.8% of revenue) is rebuilt from mid-cycle components: flat guided volumes less the project-cargo one-off, a 40% EBITDA margin (10-year mean 41.1%, FY24 trough 38%, FY22 peak 43.5%), and capex at the 10-year median 13% of revenue rather than the 5.2m maintenance-only figure the company's own 'operating free cash flow' uses. The raw FCF history is lumpy because capex is lumpy (2.5m in FY2017, 24.4m in FY2022); normalising capex is more honest than averaging the raw series.
valuation_philosophy.discount_rate: 10.0% is below the 11-12% NZ small-cap convention and above the ~8% the market has historically applied to this stock. The lower beta (0.80) is the offset for a monopoly infrastructure asset with a decade of 38-44% EBITDA margins; the +2.0pp of premiums price a NZ$80m effective float controlled by a regional council and a single-region, single-asset exposure. Tiwai concentration is priced in the bear scenario and its 25% weight, not in the rate, so it is charged once.
valuation_philosophy.terminal_value: Gordon growth at 2.25% (base) binds in all scenarios; the EV/EBITDA exit caps (8.1x/9.9x/11.4x, the stock's own 10-year min/avg/max) are recorded but do not bite because a 10% WACC already implies a terminal multiple (~5.9x EBITDA) well below the stock's history. The market_multiple_reference_iv memo (~$8.5 base) shows what the price assumes: that the historical ~10x multiple is permanent.
valuation_philosophy.what_the_price_implies: At $8.92 the base-case cash flows return ~8% - a fair-value price for an NZ income investor who treats a council-controlled port as a bond proxy and values the 4.5% gross imputed yield. It is not a price at which a 15% hurdle investor should buy (weighted entry price ~$3.4), and it leaves no margin for the three named risks: a Tiwai curtailment repeat, a Port-Planning capex cycle sized in late September 2026, and an unproven new leadership team.
valuation_philosophy.investment_framing: Income + low-single-digit growth, not a compounder. The dividend (29cps, 47% payout, fully imputed) is well covered by owner FCF (~$14m vs $7.6m paid) and is the return; multiple expansion from here has no historical precedent (10-year max P/E 19.4x on a trough base, current 14.7x on a record base).

dividend_context.history: DPS 23.0c (FY2015) -> 26.0c (FY2017-21) -> 27.0c (FY2022-24) -> 28.0c (FY2025) -> 29.0c (FY2026); never cut in the 10-year window, including the FY2024 trough.
